The Cornwall GP example data

Source: vignettes/cornwall-data.Rmd
cornwall-data.Rmd
library(spax)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

spax ships open data for general practice (GP) care in NHS Cornwall and Isles of Scilly, in south-west England. The guides use them, so this page introduces each object once: what it holds, how the objects fit together and what they cannot tell you. Nothing needs downloading.

Object What it holds How to load it
cornwall_gp 55 GP practices: location, GP workforce and list size Loaded with spax
cornwall_lsoa 337 small areas: boundaries, population and registered residents Loaded with spax
cornwall_flows Registered residents by small area and practice Loaded with spax
cornwall_travel Travel minutes from each small area to each practice Loaded with spax
cornwall_pop.tif Population grid, about 1 km cells read_spax_example()
cornwall_gp_travel.tif Travel minutes from each grid cell to each practice read_spax_example()

Each object has a help page with every column, for example ?cornwall_gp.

Practices

cornwall_gp is an sf point layer in British National Grid coordinates (EPSG:27700), one row per practice. practice is the NHS practice code, which links the practices to the flows and to the travel times.

gp <- st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)
gp |>
  select(practice, name, gp_fte_extg, gp_fte, list_size) |>
  head()
  practice                                name gp_fte_extg    gp_fte list_size
1   L82001             LANDER MEDICAL PRACTICE   10.298887 12.858887     19477
2   L82003                  PORT ISAAC SURGERY    4.693333  5.546667      8738
3   L82004 WADEBRIDGE & CAMEL ESTUARY PRACTICE    4.341333  5.194667      8045
4   L82006                      PENRYN SURGERY    7.973333  9.893333     20089
5   L82007            CAMELFORD MEDICAL CENTRE    2.888800  2.888800      6658
6   L82008             STRATTON MEDICAL CENTRE    4.670400  6.377067     10746

The guides use gp_fte_extg as supply: full-time equivalent GPs (37.5 hours a week) excluding GPs in training, from the June 2026 workforce data. GPs in training are left out because their recording changed in June 2018 and they cluster in training practices; gp_fte includes them. list_size counts all patients registered at the practice. Each practice is placed at its main site; branch surgeries are not represented.

Small areas

cornwall_lsoa holds the 337 Lower layer Super Output Areas (LSOA 2021), small areas of about 1,000 to 3,400 residents. Each has an ONS mid-2024 population estimate (pop, also by age band) and the number of its residents registered at any GP practice in England (registered). That number splits into residents registered at a practice in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly (registered_in) and those registered elsewhere (registered_out).

areas <- st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)

# Registered residents split into inside and outside the area's practices
stopifnot(all(areas$registered == areas$registered_in + areas$registered_out))

c(
  small_areas = nrow(areas),
  population = sum(areas$pop),
  registered = sum(areas$registered),
  registered_outside = sum(areas$registered_out)
)
       small_areas         population         registered registered_outside 
               337             585655             606796               5527 
# Rural-urban classification (2021), in three broad groups
table(sub(":.*", "", areas$ruc21))

 Larger rural Smaller rural         Urban 
           81           103           153

Registered counts exceed the population estimates by about 4%, reflecting list inflation and the different reference dates. The map shows the small areas by broad rural-urban class, with the practices on top.

# Small areas with a broad rural-urban class
classed <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  mutate(class = sub(":.*", "", ruc21))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = classed,
    aes(fill = class),
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = cornwall_gp, size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Rural-urban class",
    values = c(
      Urban = "#5b7fa6",
      `Larger rural` = "#a9c48f",
      `Smaller rural` = "#e3dca8"
    )
  ) +
  labs(title = "Small areas (LSOA 2021) and GP practices") +
  theme_void()

The Isles of Scilly are the small group of islands off the western tip.

Registrations

cornwall_flows counts the residents of each small area registered at each of the 55 practices, one row per pair that has at least one registration.

head(cornwall_flows)
       lsoa practice patients
1 E01018750   L82012     2185
2 E01018750   L82016       35
3 E01018750   L82025        1
4 E01018750   L82046        4
5 E01018750   L82066        1
6 E01018751   L82012     1691
# Row totals of the flows are the residents registered in the area
by_area <- tapply(cornwall_flows$patients, cornwall_flows$lsoa, sum)
stopifnot(all(by_area[areas$lsoa] == areas$registered_in))

c(
  pairs = nrow(cornwall_flows),
  registered_residents = sum(cornwall_flows$patients)
)
               pairs registered_residents 
                3188               601269

A registration is a stock: who is registered with which practice at one date (July 2026). It is not a count of visits and says nothing about how often people use their practice. Residents counted in registered_out are registered with a practice outside Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly, for example in Devon; they are not people without a practice. The allocation guides fit a model to these registrations; the FCA guides do not use them.

Travel times

cornwall_travel is a matrix of motorised travel minutes from each small area’s population-weighted centroid (rows, cornwall_lsoa$lsoa) to each practice’s main site (columns, cornwall_gp$practice).

cornwall_travel[1:3, 1:4]
          L82001 L82003 L82004 L82006
E01018750     67     49     46     78
E01018751     67     49     46     78
E01018752     68     49     47     79
# Minutes from each small area to its nearest practice
nearest <- apply(cornwall_travel, 1, min, na.rm = TRUE)
summary(nearest)
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
  1.000   1.000   1.000   2.564   3.000  13.000

The times are least-cost paths through a 2019 global friction surface with cells of about 1 km. They are rounded to whole minutes with a floor of one minute, so at least half of the small areas have a nearest practice at 1 minute. Traffic is not modelled, and in towns several practices can share one cell.

# Join each area's nearest-practice time to its polygon
nearest_map <- cornwall_lsoa |>
  mutate(minutes = nearest[lsoa])

ggplot(nearest_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = minutes), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Minutes", option = "magma", direction = -1) +
  labs(title = "Travel time to the nearest GP practice") +
  theme_void()

The grids

Two GeoTIFF files cover the same 30 arc-second grid (about 1 km, in longitude and latitude). cornwall_pop.tif holds WorldPop 2020 estimated residents per cell: a count, not a density. cornwall_gp_travel.tif holds one layer of travel minutes per practice, named by practice code. read_spax_example() reads both.

pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")
travel_grid <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")

c(
  cells = ncell(pop),
  populated_cells = sum(!is.na(values(pop))),
  travel_layers = nlyr(travel_grid),
  grid_residents = round(global(pop, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]),
  ons_residents = sum(areas$pop)
)
          cells populated_cells   travel_layers  grid_residents   ons_residents 
          35772            6985              55          542666          585655 
plot(
  pop,
  breaks = c(0, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 5000),
  col = hcl.colors(6, "YlGnBu", rev = TRUE),
  axes = FALSE,
  main = "WorldPop 2020: residents per cell (about 1 km)",
  plg = list(title = "Residents")
)

The grid total is about 7% below the ONS mid-2024 estimate used in cornwall_lsoa. The two are different sources and dates; choose one for an analysis and say which. The FCA guides use the grid; the allocation guides use registered residents of the small areas.

In the travel grid, NA marks unpopulated cells, pairs with no road connection and journeys over 180 minutes.

The Isles of Scilly and the mainland

The Isles of Scilly have one small area and one practice, St Mary’s Health Centre (L82017). The road-based travel times cannot cross the sea, so the islands and the mainland cannot reach each other: their travel times are NA.

# Unknown travel times in the small-area matrix: the Scilly area's row and
# the Scilly practice's column
c(
  unknown = sum(is.na(cornwall_travel)),
  scilly_area = sum(is.na(cornwall_travel[areas$scilly, ])),
  scilly_practice = sum(is.na(cornwall_travel[, gp$scilly]))
)
        unknown     scilly_area scilly_practice 
            390              54             336

The islands do have access to the mainland, by boat and air, which these travel times do not represent. Rather than treat the islands as cut off, the guides model mainland Cornwall only: 336 small areas and 54 practices, selected with the scilly column.

mainland_areas <- filter(areas, !scilly)
mainland_gp <- filter(gp, !scilly)
c(small_areas = nrow(mainland_areas), practices = nrow(mainland_gp))
small_areas   practices 
        336          54

In the allocation guides, mainland residents registered with the Scilly practice or outside Cornwall therefore count as registered outside mainland Cornwall. Preparing your own data shows what the unknown travel times do to an FCA index if the islands are kept.

Sources, dates and licences

Data Objects Source and date Licence
Registrations cornwall_gp, cornwall_lsoa, cornwall_flows NHS England, Patients Registered at a GP Practice, July 2026 Open Government Licence v3.0
GP workforce cornwall_gp NHS England, General Practice Workforce, 30 June 2026 Open Government Licence v3.0
Practice locations cornwall_gp ONS Postcode Directory, November 2025 Open Government Licence v3.0; contains OS and Royal Mail data
Boundaries, centroids, population cornwall_lsoa ONS LSOA 2021 boundaries and rural-urban classification, population-weighted centroids, mid-2024 population estimates Open Government Licence v3.0; contains OS data
Population grid cornwall_pop.tif WorldPop, 2020 UN-adjusted 1 km estimates Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
Travel times cornwall_travel, cornwall_gp_travel.tif Derived by the package author from the Malaria Atlas Project 2019 motorised friction surface (Weiss et al. 2020) Creative Commons Attribution; version not yet confirmed

The package’s MIT licence does not cover these data. Keep the dates in mind when reading results: the registrations and the workforce are from 2026, the population grid from 2020, the small-area population from mid-2024 and the road network from about 2019. The full attributions, with the required wording for each source, are installed with the package:

file.show(system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "spax"))
